I farm the way I know will keep the land productive without making the work too heavy for my age and family labor. I have 15 mu, but only 2 people at home and some labor goes off-farm, so I will keep the main wheat-maize rotation on 10 mu and put 5 mu into garlic, because garlic brings cash but needs more care. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed because it is steady and familiar, hybrid maize because it yields better on our land, and improved garlic cloves because I want a uniform stand and better bulbs. I will not push inputs to the maximum; I will use moderate fertilizer and a manageable number of pesticide sprays, because I want stable output and lower risk, not extra cost and labor. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage on wheat and maize land because it suits my scale and machinery access, and I will plough the garlic field because garlic needs a looser, cleaner seedbed. My goal this year is steady grain from wheat and maize for security, and garlic for income.
